title: Two known mode-frequency sums exceed orbital harmonics in 12 Kepler fits of KIC 3230227
abstract: We test exact frequency closure for two known mode groups in KIC 3230227. We fit three free frequencies with 40 orbital harmonics and quarter trends in Kepler release 25 data. Both frequency sums exceed their orbital harmonics in all 12 tests of flux product, mission half, and eclipse mask. The full corrected-flux fit with the wider mask gives offsets of 0.0001592 and 0.0001920 cycles per day. These values agree with the known near resonances. Tests with added signals recover zero and imposed nonzero offsets. The result is a check of a known system. It does not find a new mode or prove a cause. Errors depend on the stated model and time blocks. There is no independent instrument test.

display.caption: Frequency sums minus the 22nd and 26th orbital harmonics. Bars show 1.96 times the largest of the 2-day, 7-day, and 14-day block errors. These are conditional model errors.

citations.reason: Known frequencies, orbital frequency, two near-resonant sums, and physical context. We test their detuning with a separate fit and data splits.
